_note: Rules for unattended plan sessions. agy has no 'never ask, refuse instead' flag, so the runner gives each session its own throwaway HOME with a generated settings.json and hooks.json. Anything not allowed there is refused, never asked. Only commands are allowed explicitly: agy itself allows reading and writing files inside the workspace folders (the repos and the plan folder) and, as measured, also reading a file outside them, so credentials are protected by name (deny_paths), not by location. URLs and MCP tools are refused because no rule allows them. Language-neutral on purpose: all commands are allowed except the lists below. Layer 1 is the PreToolUse hook (guard.mjs + lib/rules.mjs): deny_commands, deny_paths, deny_write_paths, allow_paths, the built-in text rules, and the project scope the runner adds per run (file writes only inside the project repos, the temp folder and the session HOME; never into the plan folder except BLOCKED.md). Agent rule and doc files (.agents/rules, .claude/rules) are open; agent settings, hooks, skills and workflows are not. Layer 2 is settings_deny, written into the session's settings.json for agy to enforce by itself (RE2 regex, literal file names; wildcards in file targets are not supported). Both layers are best effort: a program that can run code can still reach what a rule refuses. The real safety is outside the session: git rollback, scope gate, secret-file gate, HEAD check, throwaway isolate database, final review. A manifest may add rules under permissions.deny: 'Bash(pattern)' adds a command rule, 'Read(glob)' and 'Edit(glob)' add path rules.
